_comment: Frontmatter key aliases. Across every surveyed tool, instruction files are markdown with optional YAML frontmatter — the parser is generic and only the key NAMES differ. Ten spellings, four meanings. A new spelling is a new row here, never a new parser.

activation_pattern._meaning: Load this file only when the agent touches files matching these globs.

activation_inclusion._meaning: Load unconditionally, regardless of what files are in play.
activation_inclusion._default_note: Absence of an activation_pattern key implies 'always' for most tools. Record which of the two produced the answer.

statement._meaning: A one-line summary the tool uses to decide relevance. Our best candidate for the claim sentence.

native_type._meaning: The source's own category label, kept verbatim. Only one tool emits this today.
native_type._verbatim_note: Never normalize this into our taxonomy in place. It is preserved so a bad mapping is a config fix rather than a republication.
native_type._observed: metadata.node_type appears in Claude Code auto-memory alongside metadata.type; treated as a type label pending confirmation.

timestamp._meaning: When the tool last wrote the record. More trustworthy than filesystem mtime.

identity._meaning: Our minted record id, written back into the source on first publication so a rename does not fork the record.

ignore._meaning: Keys we read and deliberately drop — tool bookkeeping with no bearing on the claim.
ignore._observed: metadata.originSessionId is per-session bookkeeping with no bearing on the claim.

_unknown_keys: Anything not listed above is recorded per-file in `unknown_frontmatter_keys` and surfaced in the report. That list is the alias table's own backlog — a recurring unknown key is a missing row, and the model can propose the row.
